instruction: Make the title on slide 1 bold instead of italic.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully navigated to slide 2, clicked on title placeholder, typed 'Note', selected text with Ctrl+A, right-aligned with Ctrl+R, and saved the file. Completed in 10 turns.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate between slides, click on text placeholders, type text, apply text alignment via keyboard shortcuts (Ctrl+R), and save files (Ctrl+S)
metadata.task_rationale: Tests text formatting capability. Original title on slide 1 is italic - this task requires changing it to bold and removing italic. Tests the model's ability to modify existing text formatting.
metadata.explanation: Task requires changing slide 1 title from italic to bold. Getter reads bold/italic formatting of the title text runs. Metric gives 0.5 for correct bold state and 0.5 for correct italic state.

llm_judge_reasons: Instruction requires making slide 1 title bold and removing italic. Expected values (expected_bold=true, expected_italic=false) are semantically correct.
Metric correctly handles 'rule' type expected parameter by directly accessing expected.get('expected_bold') and expected.get('expected_italic') — no incorrect nesting.
Getter reads slide index 0 (slide 1) and extracts bold/italic formatting from title placeholder text runs. Logic flow is correct.
Partial credit scoring (0.5 for bold, 0.5 for italic) provides reasonable granularity for a two-requirement task.
Postconfig saves the file (Ctrl+S) before getter reads it, ensuring fresh state.

Minor concern: run.font.bold in python-pptx can return None (inherited from style) rather than True/False. The getter treats None as False, which could give incorrect results if bold formatting is inherited from the slide master rather than set explicitly on the run.

Minor concern: Getter matches shape by name 'PlaceHolder 1' which may not match all pptx templates (common alternatives: 'Title 1', 'Title Placeholder 1'). If the name doesn't match, getter returns an error and metric scores 0.0.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider using shape.placeholder_format.idx == 0 (title placeholder index) instead of matching by shape.name == 'PlaceHolder 1' for more robust title detection.
Handle None values from run.font.bold and run.font.italic explicitly, e.g., 'if run.font.bold is True' instead of 'if run.font.bold' to distinguish between False and None (inherited).
